brands.evidence: Choose Monzo if: Your priority is daily budgeting, visualising spending habits, and easily splitting expenses
Choose Starling if: You want a completely free primary current account, you travel frequently outside Europe

client_claims.text: Monzo is a fully licensed UK bank protected by the FSCS up to £85,000
client_claims.note: Fact states FSCS protection is up to £120,000 per person, not £85,000.

client_claims.text: Monzo spending abroad: Mastercard rate, 0% fees
Monzo ATM withdrawals are fee-free in the EEA; capped at £200/30 days outside the EEA on the free tier (3% fee thereafter)
Monzo charges a £1 fee per cash deposit at PayPoint or the Post Office (free tier)
client_claims.note: No fact covers cash deposit fees.

client_claims.text: Monzo offers in-app cheque deposit photo scanning (or postal service)
Monzo has Pots, automated Salary Sorter, instant spend breakdown and round-ups
Monzo has very limited emergency web access (primarily mobile app only)
Monzo has a free tier plus paid tiers Extra, Perks and Max offering insurance, credit tracker, higher ATM limits
client_claims.note: Plan names match; benefits not covered but not contradicted.

client_claims.text: Monzo's paid tiers (Perks and Max) include travel insurance, mobile phone insurance, breakdown cover and a Greggs treat each week
Monzo is free to open with no minimum pay-in requirements
